definitions.success: task completed (run.csv success=1) AND no operator intervention (grade L0); this is the paper's "Success (no interv.)" column
definitions.outcome: success | success_with_small_intervention (task done, operator righted/moved an object, grade L2) | timeout | protective_stop (L3a, robot-triggered) | emergency_stop (L3b, operator-triggered) | failed (no stop, no timeout, task not completed)
definitions.duration_min: manifest elapsed_min = wall-clock minutes from first to last transcript message (equals the run.csv min= value where one is recorded)
definitions.output_tokens: sum of usage.output over all assistant turns of the session transcript (matches the paper and master.json tok_output_sum)
definitions.reasoning_share: thinking tokens / (thinking + visible text + tool-call argument tokens), tokenised with the archived Qwen tokenizer; reproduces the paper's Reas. column exactly
definitions.tool_calls: number of toolCall blocks in the transcript (equals manifest tool_calls_total)
definitions.motion_commands: master.json scripted_moves + hand_walked_moves (motion calls inside agent scripts + direct move tool calls); not available for second passes
definitions.second_pass: metrics computed over the transcript segment after the operator's "That worked ... Do the task again" turn

meta.run_dir_note: run_dir is the archive name under airo-archive/_decrypted/; inside it the content lives one level deeper (<run_dir>/<inner>/manifest.json). For 1e-t5 the inner dir is run-20260905T140430-1e-t5-protective-stop.

tasks.name: Cups: Red Cups
tasks.prompt: Stack the smaller red cup on top of the larger red cup.
tasks.base_skill_task: Stack the small blue cup on top of the big blue cup.

trials.note: Read both skills and the manual, located both cups in one call and batched the whole pick-and-place into a single guarded script; the profile view showed a clean two-tier stack after 4.4 min and 13 tool calls.
Re-measured the red colour window and both cup positions, touched the small cup top for its height, and stacked it in one guarded pipeline; verified concentric from the profile pose.

second_pass.note: Reused the colour window and cup height (no touch probe this time), one locate, then the same pipeline: 12 calls and 2.5 min against 24 and 7.2.

trials.note: Fastest first pass of the task (3.8 min, 18 calls): one locate, parallax correction, pad-band grasp with two closes, force-probe release and a profile-view verdict, all straight through.

second_pass.note: Reused the colour window and table height, re-measured the cup positions and the small cup top, and wrote the whole pipeline as one call: 9 calls and 1.9 min against 18 calls and 3.8 min.

trials.note: Straight run with one self-written helper script crashing once before the stack; the profile view confirmed the small cup nested on the large one after 4.0 min.

The target cup was measured about 390 px off-axis and the parallax correction under-corrected on the tapered cup, so the small cup landed on the rim shoulder and fell twice; the agent re-measured from the same biased pose and repeated the miss. The operator moved the big cup after the second fall and the trial hit the 22-min cap.

tasks.name: Cups: Large blue cups
tasks.prompt: Stack the small blue cup on top of the large blue cup.
tasks.base_skill_task: Stack the small blue cup on top of the big blue cup.

trials.note: Measured the blue colour window live (saturation separated cup from table), located both cups in one call and stacked in one guarded pipeline; verified concentric from the profile view.
One locate for both cups, touch-referenced height, pad-band grasp and force-probe release; verified from the profile view in 4.9 min.
Fastest trial of the whole grid (3.4 min, 11 calls): the agent went from skill reading to a verified stack with a single measurement script and a single pick-and-place script.

second_pass.note: Went straight to the known colour window, one locate and one touch probe, one pipeline: 4 calls and 1.8 min, the cheapest second pass.

trials.note: Located both cups in one call, applied the parallax correction and stacked in one guarded script; profile view confirmed a concentric, seated stack after 6.4 min.
Clean stack in 6.7 min with a few extra verification steps (two width checks and a profile crop) before returning the arm to the start pose.

second_pass.note: Reused the colour window but re-sampled it as a check, one locate and one touch probe; 13 calls and 2.9 min against 23 and 6.7.

tasks.name: Cups: Yellow and Green Cups
tasks.prompt: Stack the yellow cup on top of the green cup.
tasks.base_skill_task: Stack the small blue cup on top of the big blue cup.

trials.note: Slowest of the cups-only trials in calls (38): one own measurement script crashed and was rewritten, then the yellow cup was grasped and stacked on the green cup and verified top-down.
Fastest of the task (3.8 min, 16 calls): one locate, one touch probe, one pipeline script; the profile view showed the yellow dome rising above the green rim.

second_pass.note: Re-located both cups, one touch probe, stacked and verified from the profile view in 8 calls and 1.8 min.

trials.note: Located both cups from the start pose with one combined HSV window, corrected parallax and stacked; verified from the side view in 7.2 min.
One guarded pipeline (locate, touch, grasp, place); one helper script traceback was fixed on the way; stack verified after 6.8 min.
Slowest of the task (9.9 min): the top-down check was ambiguous so the agent took a profile view, which confirmed the yellow cup seated flat and concentric on the green cup.

second_pass.note: The only pass that changed its colour window (lowered the V floor); no touch probe, height inherited; 14 calls and 3.0 min against 24 and 9.9.

tasks.name: Cups: Three Cups
tasks.prompt: Stack the three cups on the table into one tower, largest at the bottom.
tasks.base_skill_task: Stack the small blue cup on top of the big blue cup.

trials.note: Located all three cups by HSV, ranked them by on-axis diameter and built the tower in two pick-and-place cycles (yellow, medium green, small green); verified 3/3 from the profile view in 8.0 min.

second_pass.note: Re-derived the colour windows on the new frame, ordered the three cups and built the tower in two cycles; 3/3 in 14 calls and 4.7 min against 22 calls and 8.0 min.

trials.note: The top cup fell during the build and the operator put it upright (small intervention); the agent re-grasped and finished a correct 3/3 tower, describing the recovery as its own. Three own-script tracebacks along the way.
Built the three-cup tower correctly in 14.2 min: located the greens in one window, two cycles with two closes 90 deg apart each, force-contact placement, profile verdict.

second_pass.note: Re-measured all three cups from scratch and rebuilt the tower correctly (3/3) in 18 calls and 5.3 min against 30 calls and 14.2 min.

trials.note: Correct 3/3 tower in 11.2 min; each cup was ordered by rim size and stacked with a force-probe release, then verified from the profile view.

Measurements were clean, but the first cycle script called gripper(width=0) (closed) where the grasp needed the jaws open and then descended blind onto the cup; the controller tripped a protective stop at z=0.025 with the jaws gripping nothing. No cup was moved (0/3).

tasks.name: Cups: Sort Cups
tasks.prompt: Arrange the four cups on the table in a straight line, from smallest to largest.
tasks.base_skill_task: Stack the small blue cup on top of the big blue cup.

trials.note: Ranked the four cups by rim diameter and placed them in a line with the reused pick-and-place primitive; verified positions with parallax-corrected fixes after 13.7 min (4/4).
Fastest of the task (12.0 min, 24 calls): four pick-and-place cycles in size order, final line red-blue-yellow-green verified numerically.

second_pass.note: Four cups re-located and lined up smallest to largest (4/4) in 9 calls and 6.0 min against 24 calls and 12.0 min.

trials.note: Slowest clean trial of the task (15.8 min): four cups placed in a straight line (4 mm y-spread) with even gaps, verified numerically and by look.

second_pass.note: Re-sampled colours, ranked the four cups and placed them in a line with 4 mm y-spread (4/4) in 17 calls and 8.0 min against 31 calls and 15.8 min.

trials.note: While laying down the blue cup it touched another cup; the force feedback opened the gripper mid-air and the cup fell tilted. The operator righted it (small intervention) and the agent finished a correct line of four.

Green, yellow and blue were placed correctly, but on the red pick the descent for the second 90-deg close brought a fingertip onto the neighbouring cup it had just placed; the arm froze in contact at 43 N and the controller tripped a protective stop (3/4).

tasks.name: Sorter: Cube
tasks.prompt: Put the blue cube into its matching hole in the shape sorter.
tasks.base_skill_task: Insert the red cylinder into the circular hole of the shape sorter.

trials.note: Identified the square hole and inserted the cube, but only after three spiral force-search scripts (about 13.6 min of robot time) when the first descents grounded above the predicted depth; seated and verified nadir after 32.7 min.
Inserted the cube into the square hole in 24.9 min with 78 calls, most of them measurement and verification; confirmed recessed from the profile and top-down views.

First aimed at the wrong opening, grounded at the predicted height, measured that opening as 47x30 mm and switched to the true 36x36 square, then fought a friction fit before the cube seated after 41.2 min.

second_pass.note: Grasped the cube centred from a nadir depth fix (avoiding the off-centre grasp of the first pass), re-identified the square by aspect ratio and seated the cube in 32 calls and 18.6 min against 105 calls and 41.2 min.

trials.note: In minute 2 the agent labelled the rectangular opening the clean square and the true square a rounded squircle, then ground the cube into the rectangle for about 50 minutes with pushes escalating to 47-60 N, re-measuring clearance nine ways but never the hole identity, until the arm tripped a protective stop.

Fastest sorter trial (12.9 min, 29 calls): measured both square-ish openings near-nadir, rejected the 44x30 rectangle, grasped the cube at theta 180 and inserted it with a force-free descent, verified recessed.

second_pass.note: The sorter had moved; the agent re-measured both square-ish openings near-nadir, rejected the rectangle and seated the cube, but an ambiguous oblique verify view cost an extra nadir look: 16.5 min, slower than its 12.9-min first pass, with half the calls (15 vs 29).

tasks.name: Sorter: Prism
tasks.prompt: Put the green triangle block into its matching hole in the shape sorter.
tasks.base_skill_task: Insert the red cylinder into the circular hole of the shape sorter.

trials.note: Grasped the prism but read it as lying on a rectangular face and commanded a 90-deg tip of the tool in mid-air; the workspace check covers only the TCP, so the arm headed toward self-collision and the operator pressed the emergency stop after 11.8 min.

The hole position came from an oblique fix on an assumed face height, so every wrist angle jammed at 12-27 N; the agent swept angle and position separately for about 40 minutes, dropped the prism four times (each righted by the operator) and reached the 68.4-min cap without inserting.

Same plan as t1: tip the held prism 90 deg in the air and set it down on a triangular face. The set-down with a horizontal tool axis drove the gripper body into the table and the controller tripped a protective stop; the agent then correctly diagnosed the dead RTDE program and began restarting the service.

The sorter had been staged just past the top-down reach envelope. After a reach survey the agent decided to drag the sorter by its door handle, pushed the open jaws into its front face (12.7 N) and ended in a pose with no IK escape; the controller tripped a protective stop after 32.8 min.

Only prism success: two near-nadir ray fixes agreed on the hole, the local face height was touched (0.051, not the skill constant 0.045), and the wrist was swept over the hole for the force minimum (0.1 N at 249 deg) before a force-free descent seated the prism in 32.0 min.

second_pass.note: Two near-nadir fixes agreed on the hole, the local face height 0.051 was reused and the prism seated in 32 calls and 9.7 min against 85 calls and 32.0 min.

tasks.name: Sorter: Beam
tasks.prompt: Put the yellow rectangular block into its matching hole in the shape sorter.
tasks.base_skill_task: Insert the red cylinder into the circular hole of the shape sorter.

trials.note: Identified the 44x26 mm block and its rectangular hole, aligned the yaw and inserted it, but the camera stream froze after the release and about 18 minutes went to diagnosing and restarting the platform service; the model also served at about a third of normal speed. Verified seated after 67.5 min.

second_pass.note: Immediately checked the block orientation on the table, gripped it at that angle, moved over the rectangular hole and inserted it: 22 calls and 8.0 min against 88 calls and 67.5 min.

trials.note: Inserted the beam in the rectangular hole after force-search sweeps and verified it recessed; the operator physically rescued an object once during the run (grade corrected to a small intervention after scoring), so it does not count as a clean success.

Seated the beam in the rectangular hole after 43.8 min and 87 calls, with four own-script tracebacks and long attempts to read the held block angle from a cut-off frame; one small operator intervention during the run.

Measured the block as 49x33, 46x29 then 40x26 mm and the hole as 29x37, 36x34, 42x39 then 42x42 mm over 46 minutes, concluded it fits, and descended with the gripper open straight onto the sorter; protective stop.
Identified the block and the four holes by rectangle fill, grasped across the long side, aligned and inserted with a force-free descent; verified recessed from an oblique crop after 38.4 min.

second_pass.note: Failed: the agent drove the gripper into the robot body, leaving the arm in a twisted joint configuration that the UR driver would not move out of; scored as a protective stop after 43 calls and 19.2 min.

tasks.name: Rings
tasks.prompt: Stack all the rings on the table onto the rod to rebuild the tower, largest at the bottom.
objects_on_table: five rings (teal, blue, yellow, white, pink)
tasks.base_skill_task: Grasp the largest (teal) ring and put it on the rod.

trials.note: Spent about 45 minutes before the first pick (20 deciding whether the rod was vertical, 25 debugging diameter scripts), then measured the pink ring larger than the white from oblique views and stacked pink under white. The agent reported a correct tower; the trial is scored a failure (prefix 3/5).
Threaded three rings, then the white-ring detector returned the yellow ring / the stack on the rod; the arm went for it and drove itself into the rod, tripping a protective stop after 17.8 min (3/5).
Fastest rings success (22.8 min, 51 calls): flew the camera over each ring for on-axis diameters, ordered them, and threaded all five with clean cycles; verified from a wide side view.

second_pass.note: The largest ring slipped out of the grasp repeatedly (five failed grasps) before the agent adjusted; once it held, the other four rings went on quickly. 55 calls and 34.2 min, slower than the 22.8-min first pass.

trials.note: Correct five-ring tower in 26.4 min; verified concentric and in descending size order from the side view before returning home.
Correct tower in 33.1 min; the agent noticed the base had slid about 12 mm when the first ring landed and re-anchored the rod fix on every cycle.

second_pass.note: Went fast, noticed on its own that the white-ring measurement was off, re-measured it and finished the tower smoothly: 37 calls and 15.6 min against 83 calls and 33.1 min.

second_pass_totals.rank_transfer: 6 of 8 tasks with two second passes: the resume of the faster first pass was again the faster one
